title: Research Participant Registry "Hopkins Opportunities for Participant Engagement"
official: "HOPE" Research Participant Registry "Hopkins Opportunities for Participant Engagement"
summary:
The HOPE (Hopkins Opportunities for Participant Engagement) Research Registry is a free and secure way for adults to learn about research studies at Johns Hopkins and find out about opportunities to participate. HOPE was created to help connect people who are interested in research with Johns Hopkins research teams conducting studies in many different health areas.

Adults age 18 or older who live in the United States may voluntarily join HOPE. To enroll, participants complete a short form that takes about 5 minutes and provide basic information about themselves and the types of research the participant may be interested in. Participants may receive information about new research studies, including studies related to the topics selected.

If a participant is interested in a study, the participant can choose to share contact information with the research team so the team can contact the participant directly. Joining HOPE does not mean that a person has to participate in any research study. Participation in HOPE is voluntary, there is no cost to join, and participants can update information or leave the registry at any time.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older
* Resides in the United States
* Apple to provide informed consent
* Interested in learning about research opportunities and/or receiving research updates
* Able to read English

Exclusion Criteria:

* Under 18 years of age
* Unable to provide informed consent
* Resides outside of the United States
